content: Approximately 30-40% of individuals who contract COVID-19 experience symptoms that persist for four weeks or longer, a condition commonly referred to as Long COVID or post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC). For individuals with pre-existing diabetes, this condition can lead to ongoing or recurrent health issues, which may exacerbate their overall health status. People with diabetes are at an increased risk of developing complications due to Long COVID, which can affect multiple organs and metabolic systems. As a result, individuals with diabetes may require long-term medical follow-up and care to manage these complications effectively. Those with poor glucose control are particularly vulnerable and may need more frequent monitoring to address the heightened risk of adverse outcomes.
